Compute CDR3 amino acid convergence scores across neighbourhoods

Source: R/nhood_cdr3_convergence.R
nhood_cdr3_convergence.Rd

Computes a per neighbourhood summary convergence statistic of pairwise CDR3 amino acid sequence distances between B cell receptor (BCR) or T cell receptor (TCR) clones.

Usage

nhood_cdr3_convergence(
  object,
  nhood_col = NULL,
  receptor_type = c("BCR", "TCR"),
  chain = c("VDJ", "VJ", "both"),
  aa_col,
  clone_id_col = NULL,
  min_n_contigs = 20L,
  min_clones = NULL,
  distance_method = c("levenshtein", "blosum62", "custom"),
  substitution_matrix = NULL,
  summary_metric = "converge_score",
  knn_k = NULL,
  downsample = TRUE,
  n_boots = 100,
  seed = NULL,
  BPPARAM = BiocParallel::SerialParam(),
  result_name = "nhood_cdr3_convergence"
)

Arguments

object

A Milo or SingleCellExperiment object. Seurat objects must first be converted via as.SingleCellExperiment.

nhood_col

Character string. For plain SingleCellExperiment objects (i.e. not Milo), the name of the colData column containing neighbourhood assignments. Not required for Milo objects.

receptor_type

Character string; one of "BCR" (default) or "TCR". Controls clone-level representative selection: for BCR, a centroid sequence is chosen per clone (the sequence with the lowest mean pairwise distance to all other members of the same clone). For TCR, unique sequences are used directly as representatives. Ignored if clone_id_col is NULL.

chain

Character string; one of "VDJ" (default), "VJ", or "both". Determines which receptor chain(s) are analysed. When chain = "both", aa_col must be a named character vector with elements "VDJ" and "VJ" (see aa_col).

aa_col

Character string or named character vector specifying the colData column(s) containing CDR3 amino acid sequences. When chain is "VDJ" or "VJ", supply a single column name. When chain = "both", supply a named vector with elements "VDJ" and "VJ", e.g.: aa_col = c(VDJ = "cdr3_aa_heavy", VJ = "cdr3_aa_light"). Cells with NA, empty string, "No_contig", or "None" in the relevant column are excluded from analysis.

clone_id_col

Character string; name of the colData column containing clone identifiers (e.g. output from a clonotyping tool). When supplied and receptor_type = "BCR", one centroid sequence is selected per clone per neighbourhood. When NULL (default), all unique CDR3 sequences are treated as individual representatives regardless of receptor_type. If the column is not found in colData, a warning is issued and the function falls back to unique-sequence mode.

min_n_contigs

Integer; minimum number of cells with valid contig annotation required for a neighbourhood to be included in the analysis. Neighbourhoods below this threshold are assigned NA for all distance metrics and converge_score_reliable = FALSE. Default is 20. When min_clones is also supplied, setting min_n_contigs below that value gives it no independent gating effect; a warning is issued in this case.

min_clones

Integer or NULL (default). When supplied, neighbourhoods with fewer representative sequences than this threshold are excluded: all metrics are set to NA and converge_score_reliable = FALSE. When NULL, all neighbourhoods that pass min_n_contigs are processed regardless of representative count. Must be at least equal to min_n_contigs to have any independent gating effect; a warning is issued otherwise. converge_score may be unstable when n_clones is small relative to \(k\): when the adaptive \(k\) approaches n_clones, each sequence's nearest neighbours span nearly the entire neighbourhood and the kNN score converges toward the global mean. If this is a concern, set min_clones to a value comfortably above the adaptive \(k\) floor (e.g. 20) to exclude such neighbourhoods, or inspect <chain>_n_clones in the output to identify small neighbourhoods post-hoc. converge_score is reported as NA only when n_clones <= resolved_k, since kNN cannot be computed when there are insufficient sequences to form a neighbourhood.

distance_method

Character string; one of "levenshtein" (default), "blosum62", or "custom".

"levenshtein"

Flat substitution cost: 0 for identical amino acids, 1 for any mismatch, normalised by the length of the longer sequence. Equivalent to normalised edit distance.

"blosum62"

Substitution cost derived from BLOSUM62 via \(c(i,j) = (s(i,i) + s(j,j)) / 2 - s(i,j)\), normalised to \([0, 1]\) by the maximum off-diagonal cost. Biochemically similar amino acids incur lower cost than dissimilar ones.

"custom"

User-supplied substitution matrix passed via substitution_matrix. Must follow the same sign convention as pwalign::stringDist (higher score = more similar). See substitution_matrix.

substitution_matrix

A square numeric matrix with named rows and columns (single-letter amino acid codes) to use when distance_method = "custom". The matrix must follow the pwalign::stringDist sign convention: higher values indicate more similar amino acids (i.e. a score matrix, not a cost matrix). Ignored unless distance_method = "custom".

summary_metric

Character vector; one or more of "converge_score" (default), "converge_score_global", and "converge_score_global_median". Controls which summary convergence metrics are calculated and returned:

"converge_score"

kNN convergence score per neighbourhood. Captures local sequence density. NA when n_clones <= resolved_k (kNN cannot be computed), or when min_clones is supplied and not met.

"converge_score_global"

Mean pairwise CDR3 convergence score across the upper triangle of the representative distance matrix.

"converge_score_global_median"

Median pairwise CDR3 convergence score across the upper triangle of the representative distance matrix.

Any combination of the three values may be supplied. The default is "converge_score".

knn_k

Integer or NULL (default). Number of nearest neighbours to use when computing converge_score. When NULL, \(k\) is set adaptively to \(\lfloor 0.25 \times n_{\text{reps}} \rfloor\) per neighbourhood. A floor of 3 ensures the metric captures more than just the nearest pairwise comparisons. When a fixed integer is supplied it is used as-is with no clamping applied. Within each bootstrap subsample \(k\) is additionally capped at \(n - 1\) to guard against subsamples smaller than \(k\).

downsample

Logical; whether to downsample large neighbourhoods to a common representative depth before computing distances. The downsampling depth is set to the median number of unique representatives across all passing neighbourhoods (excluding singletons), computed separately per chain. Downsampling is performed via bootstrapping (n_boots iterations). Default is TRUE. When FALSE, the full representative matrix is used directly and _sd columns are not reported.

n_boots

Integer; number of bootstrap iterations used during downsampling. Each iteration subsamples downsample_depth representatives without replacement and computes distance summaries; reported values are the mean across iterations and the corresponding _sd column reports the standard deviation across iterations for each requested metric. Default is 100. Ignored when downsample = FALSE or when a neighbourhood has fewer representatives than the downsampling depth. When downsample = TRUE and "converge_score" is in summary_metric, the effective sample size for kNN computation within each bootstrap iteration is the downsampling depth rather than the full representative count. If this depth is \(\leq\) \(k\), converge_score will be NA for all downsampled neighbourhoods and a warning is emitted. In this scenario, set downsample = FALSE or use summary_metric = "converge_score_global" to obtain values for all neighbourhoods.

seed

Integer or NULL (default). Random seed for reproducibility of the bootstrap downsampling procedure. When supplied, a neighbourhood-specific seed is derived as seed + i (where i is the neighbourhood index), ensuring that each neighbourhood's bootstrap is independently reproducible while the full run remains deterministic. Set this parameter whenever results will be reported or compared across runs. Has no effect when downsample = FALSE.

BPPARAM

A BiocParallelParam instance controlling parallelisation. The default, SerialParam(), runs sequentially with per-neighbourhood progress messages. Parallel backends (e.g. MulticoreParam, SnowParam) suppress per-neighbourhood messages but respect all other arguments. Note that when using process-based parallel backends, all data objects are serialised to each worker, which may increase peak memory usage substantially for large datasets.

result_name

Character string; the key under which results are stored in metadata(object). If an entry with this name already exists a warning is emitted and the entry is overwritten. Default is "nhood_cdr3_convergence".

Value

The input object with a data.frame added to metadata(object)[[result_name]]. The data.frame has one row per neighbourhood and the following columns:

nhood

Neighbourhood identifier.

nhood_size

Total number of cells in the neighbourhood, including cells without a contig. Used as the denominator for contig_capture_rate.

<chain>_n_contigs

Number of cells with a contig for this chain.

<chain>_contig_capture_rate

Proportion of neighbourhood cells with a contig (n_contigs / nhood_size). NA if nhood_size is zero.

<chain>_n_clones

Number of representative sequences used for distance computation (unique sequences for contigs without clone labels; one centroid per clone for BCR with clone labels).

<chain>_converge_score_reliable

Logical; FALSE when n_contigs < min_n_contigs (all metrics NA), or when min_clones is supplied and n_clones does not meet it (all metrics NA). TRUE for all other neighbourhoods, including those where converge_score is NA due to insufficient sequences for kNN.

CDR3_converge_score_<chain>

kNN convergence score per neighbourhood, averaged across all representatives. Captures local sequence density. When downsampling, this is the mean across bootstrap iterations. NA when n_clones <= resolved_k (insufficient sequences for kNN), or when min_clones is supplied and n_clones does not meet it. Only present when "converge_score" is in summary_metric. Example: CDR3_converge_score_VDJ.

CDR3_converge_score_sd_<chain>

Standard deviation of CDR3_converge_score_<chain> across bootstrap iterations. Only present when downsample = TRUE and "converge_score" is in summary_metric. NA when converge_score is NA (kNN could not be computed). Example: CDR3_converge_score_sd_VDJ.

CDR3_converge_score_global_<chain>

Mean pairwise CDR3 convergence score across the upper triangle of the representative distance matrix. When downsampling, this is the mean across bootstrap iterations. Only present when "converge_score_global" is in summary_metric. Example: CDR3_converge_score_global_VDJ.

CDR3_converge_score_global_sd_<chain>

Standard deviation of CDR3_converge_score_global_<chain> across bootstrap iterations. Only present when downsample = TRUE and "converge_score_global" is in summary_metric. Example: CDR3_converge_score_global_sd_VDJ.

CDR3_converge_score_global_median_<chain>

Median pairwise CDR3 convergence score across the upper triangle of the representative distance matrix. When downsampling, this is the mean of bootstrap-iteration medians. Only present when "converge_score_global_median" is in summary_metric. Example: CDR3_converge_score_global_median_VJ.

CDR3_converge_score_global_median_sd_<chain>

Standard deviation of CDR3_converge_score_global_median_<chain> across bootstrap iterations. Only present when downsample = TRUE and "converge_score_global_median" is in summary_metric. Example: CDR3_converge_score_global_median_sd_VDJ.

Where chain = "both", columns are present for both VDJ and VJ chains.

The returned data.frame also carries the following attributes recording the analysis parameters: receptor_type, distance_method, chains, downsample_depths, min_n_contigs, min_clones, downsample, n_boots, summary_metric.

Details

Distance computation pipeline

For each neighbourhood the following steps are performed:

  1. Cells are filtered to those with valid CDR3 annotation.

  2. A single pairwise distance matrix is computed over all unique CDR3 sequences. Distances are normalised to \([0, 1]\) by dividing each raw pairwise distance by the length of the longer sequence in that pair.

  3. For BCR data with clone labels, one centroid sequence is selected per clone as the sequence with the lowest mean pairwise distance to all other unique sequences within that clone in the neighbourhood. The raw pairwise distance matrix is filtered to these centroids.

  4. If downsample = TRUE and the number of representatives exceeds the target depth, bootstrapped subsampling is performed over the pre-computed distance matrix (no re-alignment), and summary statistics are averaged across iterations.

Supported distance methods

The function supports three distance methods: Levenshtein edit distance, BLOSUM62-derived substitution cost, and a user-supplied custom matrix, all normalised to 0-1 by the length of the longer sequence in each pair.

Downsampling depth

Downsampling is recommended where neighbourhood sizes differ substantially to ensure distances are comparable across neighbourhoods. The downsampling depth is the median number of unique representatives across all neighbourhoods that pass min_n_contigs, excluding singleton- representative neighbourhoods. This is computed separately per chain when chain = "both", as VDJ and VJ clone counts can differ. The depth is reported in the progress messages emitted to the console.

Neighbourhood size and capture rate

nhood_size and contig_capture_rate are based on all cells assigned to the neighbourhood in the binary nhoods matrix, regardless of contig annotation status. This reflects the overall cellular composition of the neighbourhood rather than immune cell abundance alone, and is the intended denominator for capture rate.

Parallelisation

Each neighbourhood is processed independently and dispatched as a separate task via bplapply. With SerialParam (default), progress is reported at every 10\ progress is suppressed; a completion summary is printed after collation.

See also

pwalign::stringDist() for the underlying alignment engine. BiocParallelParam for parallelisation options. nhood_diversity, nhood_shm, nhood_annotation, nhood_annotation_props

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
# --- Milo object, BCR, VDJ chain only, Levenshtein distance -------------
milo <- nhood_cdr3_convergence(
  object        = milo_object,
  receptor_type = "BCR",
  chain         = "VDJ",
  aa_col        = "cdr3_aa_heavy",
  clone_id_col  = "clone_id",
  seed          = 42
)
results <- S4Vectors::metadata(milo)$nhood_cdr3_convergence

# --- Milo object, TCR, both chains, BLOSUM62, all metrics ----------------
milo <- nhood_cdr3_convergence(
  object          = milo_object,
  receptor_type   = "TCR",
  chain           = "both",
  aa_col          = c(VDJ = "cdr3_aa_TRB", VJ = "cdr3_aa_TRA"),
  distance_method = "blosum62",
  summary_metric  = c("converge_score", "converge_score_global", "converge_score_global_median"),
  min_n_contigs     = 5,
  seed            = 42,
  BPPARAM         = BiocParallel::MulticoreParam(workers = 4)
)

# --- SingleCellExperiment object, BCR, custom substitution matrix --------
custom_mat <- matrix(...)  # 20x20 numeric, named by single-letter AA code
sce <- nhood_cdr3_convergence(
  object              = sce_object,
  receptor_type       = "BCR",
  chain               = "VDJ",
  aa_col              = "cdr3_aa_heavy",
  clone_id_col        = "clone_id",
  nhood_col           = "nhood_id",
  distance_method     = "custom",
  substitution_matrix = custom_mat,
  seed                = 42
)
} # }
